habitat: Groups of two to five in acacia woodland, feeding in the canopy.
summary: A common resident. A brown throat-bar, when present, is distinctive. Otherwise it is told by pale yellow-buff underparts and a pale eye with a brown surround. Newman’s size field was unusable, so no length was stored. The call is a rapid teeup-ti-ti-ti-ti followed by a short trill.

similar.note: Yellow-bellied Eremomela has a grey breast, a yellow belly and black soft parts. Burnt-necked Eremomela has pale yellow-buff underparts and a pale eye.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^14=16384 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 8192–32768.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Pale eye with a brown surround. A brown throat-bar is not always present.

viewNotes.note: Small canopy bird in acacia, with a pale eye.
Pale eye and brown eye-ring. The brown throat-bar may be absent.
The back colour was not named.

calls.description: A rapid, high-pitched teeup-ti-ti-ti-ti-ti-ti-ti, followed by a short trill. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Kruger. The filename is 1020_cut and the catalogue type is song.
